clue.text: Laboured and noisy, finding trousers almost too tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone squeezed into trousers that are a size too small is puffing and panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last O of TOO, leaving TO; 'tight' (drunk) is the anagram signal for TROUSERS plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stertorous breathing is heavy snoring-like respiration, which is both laboured and loud.

clue.text: You work best when on this number

definitions.text: You work best when on this number

parts.words: You work best when on this number
parts.note: the idiom 'on' this sort of musical number means performing at the top of your form

explanation.definitionFit: Being 'on song' is a British idiom for playing or working at your very best, and a song is a musical number.

clue.text: Commonly uses microwave for snacks

indicators.note: common, uneducated speech is stereotyped as dropping its initial aitches

parts.note: to use a microwave is to heat food, giving heats

explanation.surface: Ordinary people tend to zap their quick bites in the microwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' signals the dropped H of Cockney speech, so HEATS becomes 'EATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, especially light meals or snacks.

clue.text: Appropriate newspapers may be found in hotel room

definitions.text: may be found in hotel room

parts.note: to trouser money is slang for pocketing or appropriating it
the press is newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Suitable newspapers are left for guests in the bedroom of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb: to trouser is to pocket something.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for creasing slacks is a standard fitting in many British hotel bedrooms.

clue.text: Garden implement lacking handle needs spiked wheel

indicators.note: the handle of a word is taken as its first letter, here removed

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool for gardening

explanation.surface: A broken trowel without its handle needs a spiky wheel replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking handle' removes the first letter T from TROWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small revolving toothed disc on the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: Dithering dunce died in a muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a confused jumble, signalling these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A slow pupil, confused and dying, cannot make up his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dithering is wavering and has not yet made a choice.

clue.text: Plays in book form

definitions.meaning: performs on stage, as an actor does
the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Theatre pieces published as a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts means performs a role, and it is also the short name of a New Testament book.

clue.text: Very old driver in good spirits about a commotion

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: cheer is happiness or good spirits
a riot is an uproar or commotion

explanation.surface: An elderly motorist in high spirits is caught up in a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' is part of the definition: an ancient chariot driver, not an elderly motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A charioteer drove an ancient chariot, so he is a driver from the very distant past.

clue.text: Absolutely no movement in shares yet

parts.note: stock means shares in a company
still means yet, as in 'still to come'

explanation.surface: The stock market is completely flat, with share prices not budging.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means utterly motionless.

clue.text: Race so open, when across country?

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
wide means open, as in a door left wide

explanation.surface: A competition so open that runners spread across the whole land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means extending throughout an entire country.

clue.text: Half-hearted call for attention, giving a light ring

indicators.note: half of the heart of the word is lost: one of its two middle letters goes

parts.note: hallo is a shout to attract someone's attention

explanation.surface: A feeble shout to someone gives them a quick phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two central Ls of HALLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light, as round a saint's head or the moon.

clue.text: Cutting employment without offence to Party in the lead

indicators.note: in the lead means this piece is placed in front

parts.note: Labour is a major UK political party
saving, as in 'saving your presence', is an old phrase meaning without offence to

explanation.surface: A party leading the polls promises to cut jobs without upsetting anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving your reverence' is an old apology, so saving = without offence to.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour-saving machinery reduces the amount of work people must do, cutting the need for workers.

clue.text: Threatening, for instance, to boycott a sort of school

parts.note: as means for instance, as in 'cities such as'
to black goods is to boycott them in a trade union dispute
a sink school is a British term for a failing school in a deprived area

explanation.surface: Union members threaten to boycott a run-down school.
explanation.walkthrough: A sink school is British slang for a failing state school in a poor area.
explanation.definitionFit: Skies as black as ink look ominous, so the phrase describes something threatening.

clue.text: Selfish concierge takes time to turn out

indicators.note: to turn out means to be rearranged into a different form

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A hotel porter takes his time to emerge, thinking only of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn out' scrambles CONCIERGE plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric means centred on oneself, which is a synonym for selfish.

clue.text: A short Australian chap can be biting

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Strine is a humorous name for Australian English
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A diminutive man from Down Under can make cutting remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts STRINE (a joke spelling of 'Australian' as said by Australians) to STRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and severe, which is what biting means.

clue.text: Put foot down about work after anaesthetic, as a sluggish type

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the gas

parts.note: gas is used as an anaesthetic, eg by dentists

indicators.note: about means the word for a step goes around the other piece

parts.note: trod means stepped, put one's foot down
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A patient firmly insists on surgery after being given gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put foot down' looks like accelerating or insisting, but it means trod. 'sluggish type' is literal: slugs are gastropods.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastropods are molluscs such as slugs and snails, so a slug is literally a sluggish type.

clue.text: Make poor Iolanthe wait outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for a wait goes around the other

parts.note: a pause is a short wait
Iolanthe is the fairy, or peri, of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera 'The Peer and the Peri'

explanation.surface: A fairy told to wait might fall on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is the fairy heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera subtitled 'The Peer and the Peri'; a peri is a Persian fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pauperise someone is to reduce them to poverty.

clue.text: Group takes time in church being absorbed in scripture

indicators.note: absorbed in means held within the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A band takes time out in church, engrossed in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is the definition; both containers nest, the church letters with time inside going into the scripture letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially musicians.

clue.text: One tending to be short of energy in a rush

indicators.note: short of means one letter is missing from the word

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A busy person tends to run short of energy when hurrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be short of' removes an E from CAREER.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after or tends to a sick or elderly person.

clue.text: Waterproofing submarine finds vital in the end

parts.note: submarine means under the sea

indicators.note: in the end means only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A submarine finds a watertight coat essential in the long run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' is the adjective (undersea), not the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Underseal is a protective coating applied to a car's underside against water and rust.

clue.text: Not required, aliens sent on manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are tactical movements, signalling the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Extraterrestrials sent on exercises are surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as part of 'on manoeuvres' but is fodder; 'manoeuvres' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonessential means not necessary, so it is a synonym for not required.

clue.text: Negotiate with a party

definitions.meaning: an outing or celebration laid on for others

explanation.surface: Bargain with a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Treat means to negotiate, and a treat is an entertainment given for others.

clue.text: Not in favour of some hard liquor

parts.note: a, as in 'a drink', means some
gin is a strong spirit

explanation.surface: A teetotaller opposes any amount of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is dialect for against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Said to be taking alternate goes in four-ball

indicators.note: taking alternate goes means every other letter is used

explanation.surface: Golfers playing four-ball are said to take turns.
explanation.walkthrough: A four-ball is a golf match of two pairs; take letters 2, 4, 6 and 8.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken, so it means said aloud rather than written.

clue.text: Smell from speaker's overturned drink

indicators.note: speaker's means the word as pronounced

parts.note: kir, a French aperitif of white wine and cassis, turned backwards; the French i is said 'ee'

explanation.surface: A whiff comes from a drink knocked over by a public speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir is said 'keer', so its backwards spelling, read with the same French vowel, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reek is a strong unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Handy description of Virginia creeper?

parts.note: the plant's leaves split into five leaflets like a hand, so the name it carries describes a hand

explanation.definitionFit: Five-finger is a folk name given to plants with palmate leaves of five leaflets, Virginia creeper among them.

clue.text: Vision with sound, for instance

indicators.note: with sound means the word for vision is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A film offering pictures plus a soundtrack, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: to cite is to give as an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to quote or mention it as an example.

clue.text: Plan old agent devised, covering several angles

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A veteran spy's scheme considers every possibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' scrambles PLAN, O and AGENT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagonal shape has five angles, which is several.
